core.topic: Creative direction, themes, and design pillars
core.finding: [CONFIRMED] Rockstar's official synopsis frames the game around CJ returning to Los Santos, family crisis, gang trouble and a journey across San Andreas.
core.implementation_or_verification: Use a distinct original protagonist, family stakes and district-spanning escalation; test that each chapter changes location, cast or world-state.
core.scope: PS2 2004 baseline; source-specific platform caveats retained

core.topic: Studio organization, credits, and production roles
core.finding: [SECONDARY] The PS2 credit transcription attributes producer, art direction, technical direction, city art leads, animation, audio and QA roles to named staff; credit lists are role evidence, not a complete org chart.
core.implementation_or_verification: Keep separate accountable owners for world art, characters, animation, vehicles, missions, audio, tools and QA. Do not infer reporting lines from credit order.
core.scope: PS2 2004 baseline; source-specific platform caveats retained

core.topic: Engine, middleware, and runtime architecture
core.finding: [CONFIRMED] Former technical director Obbe Vermeij states that GTA III, Vice City and San Andreas ran on RenderWare; he also says the post-SA transition to RAGE required new shader work.
core.implementation_or_verification: Do not clone RenderWare. The Web project uses Godot 4.7 Compatibility/WebGL2; validate render features against the browser target.
core.scope: PS2 2004 baseline; source-specific platform caveats retained

core.topic: Build tools, asset pipeline, and runtime data
core.finding: [UNKNOWN] The inspected public sources do not establish the full proprietary source-asset conversion chain, exact build tooling or data schema used for the 2004 PS2 build.
core.implementation_or_verification: Adopt an explicit original pipeline: DCC source → licensed export → import validation → runtime data → packaged Web chunks; store provenance and hashes.
core.scope: PS2 2004 baseline; source-specific platform caveats retained

core.topic: Whole-world geography, progression gates, and spatial hierarchy
core.finding: [CONFIRMED] Rockstar's synopsis and developer Q&A describe a continuous state-scale experience spanning three cities and countryside; the 2006 developer answer gives a 6 km × 6 km outside-map estimate, with interiors excluded.
core.implementation_or_verification: Build the original world as streamed sectors, not one giant always-resident scene; measure sector residency and transition hitches.
core.scope: PS2 2004 baseline; source-specific platform caveats retained

core.topic: Los Santos: districts, landmarks, routes, and gameplay identity
core.finding: [CONFIRMED] Los Santos is the opening/home city in Rockstar's official synopsis; its role is tied to CJ's return and family/gang conflict.
core.implementation_or_verification: Give Harbor City an authored opening loop with a safe learning route, landmark chain and mission-critical home district.
core.scope: PS2 2004 baseline; source-specific platform caveats retained

core.topic: San Fierro: districts, landmarks, routes, and gameplay identity
core.finding: [CONFIRMED] San Fierro is one of the three named cities in the secondary database's baseline summary; exact PS2 district inventory is not established in the sources inspected here.
core.implementation_or_verification: Give Sapphire Coast a different road topology and silhouette language; require region-specific landmarks and route tests.
core.scope: PS2 2004 baseline; source-specific platform caveats retained

core.topic: Las Venturas: districts, landmarks, routes, and gameplay identity
core.finding: [CONFIRMED] Las Venturas is named as one of the three cities in the database summary; a PS2-only full venue inventory was not checked.
core.implementation_or_verification: Give Amber Valley a distinct night/economy identity, but do not borrow GTA map geometry or business names.
core.scope: PS2 2004 baseline; source-specific platform caveats retained

core.topic: Countryside, desert, water, and transitional spaces
core.finding: [CONFIRMED] The 2006 developer answer says the player can travel beyond populated areas by boat or plane; it excludes interiors from the 6×6 km outside-map figure.
core.implementation_or_verification: Model coast, rural space, desert-like open space and air/water traversal as separate traversal domains with their own boundaries and streaming tests.
core.scope: PS2 2004 baseline; source-specific platform caveats retained

core.topic: Roads, intersections, paths, lanes, and traversal networks
core.finding: [CONFIRMED] The developer Q&A describes map sections with object-count ceilings that constrained density; it does not provide a complete road graph.
core.implementation_or_verification: Represent streets as a navigable graph with lane direction, speed class and junction rules; profile actor density per sector.
core.scope: PS2 2004 baseline; source-specific platform caveats retained

core.topic: Interiors, access rules, portals, and transitions
core.finding: [CONFIRMED] The same developer answer says the outside-map measurement excludes many interior locations; exact portal implementation is not disclosed.
core.implementation_or_verification: Use explicit interior scene IDs, entry/exit transforms and save-safe transition transactions; verify no duplicate player or NPC after transition.
core.scope: PS2 2004 baseline; source-specific platform caveats retained

core.topic: World sectors, asset streaming, loading, and residency
core.finding: [CONFIRMED] A developer describes shared low-detail building models loaded as the player moves, replacing a previous island-transition-style load pattern.
core.implementation_or_verification: Build per-sector visual proxies/LOD groups and stream them around the camera; assert bounded resident mesh/texture counts during a long drive.
core.scope: PS2 2004 baseline; source-specific platform caveats retained

core.topic: Population zones, spawns, density, and despawns
core.finding: [UNKNOWN] No reliable PS2-build spawn radius, population cap or despawn rule was established from inspected sources.
core.implementation_or_verification: Use spawn volumes keyed by district and distance bands; record spawn/despawn reasons and test deterministic actor budgets.
core.scope: PS2 2004 baseline; source-specific platform caveats retained

core.topic: Civilian movement, perception, and reactions
core.finding: [UNKNOWN] The inspected primary materials do not define civilian perception cones, reaction tables or pedestrian pathfinding algorithms.
core.implementation_or_verification: Build civilian state machines with explicit idle/walk/avoid/flee/talk states; test obstacle avoidance, reaction cooldowns and actor cleanup.
core.scope: PS2 2004 baseline; source-specific platform caveats retained

core.topic: Gangs, faction relationships, and territorial control
core.finding: [CONFIRMED] The official synopsis explicitly references gang trouble; the PS2 manual lists a gang active/passive control mode and a map legend including territory.
core.implementation_or_verification: Implement faction relationship data and zone-control state separate from individual NPC AI; test territory changes against mission state.
core.scope: PS2 2004 baseline; source-specific platform caveats retained

core.topic: Fictional law enforcement, wanted levels, and escalation
core.finding: [UNKNOWN] A precise wanted-level escalation algorithm for the specified PS2 regional build was not established here.
core.implementation_or_verification: Implement an original heat score with witness/visibility decay, dispatch stages and safe-state reset; test line-of-sight loss and zone transitions.
core.scope: PS2 2004 baseline; source-specific platform caveats retained

core.topic: Player controls, locomotion, traversal, and interaction
core.finding: [CONFIRMED] The PS2 manual separates on-foot, bicycle, car, first-person shooting, swimming, helicopter and plane controls; movement and actions are context-dependent.
core.implementation_or_verification: Use a player control-state router; only the active locomotion/vehicle mode may consume mutually exclusive actions.
core.scope: PS2 2004 baseline; source-specific platform caveats retained

core.topic: Camera behavior, aiming, framing, and obstruction handling
core.finding: [CONFIRMED] The manual assigns camera center, camera modes, look-behind and right-analog camera movement to distinct actions.
core.implementation_or_verification: Implement camera orbit/aim/look-back as explicit modes; test obstruction sweeps and ensure camera motion never feeds back into locomotion unintentionally.
core.scope: PS2 2004 baseline; source-specific platform caveats retained

core.topic: Health, armor, recovery, and failure states
core.finding: [CONFIRMED] The PS2 guide references hospital recovery after street failure, but no exact health/armor formula was measured in this research pass.
core.implementation_or_verification: Define downed/dead/recovery states and preserve mission-critical world state across recovery; test restart and reward duplication.
core.scope: PS2 2004 baseline; source-specific platform caveats retained

core.topic: Player attributes, skills, body changes, and progression
core.finding: [UNKNOWN] Exact attribute progression, body-change thresholds and statistical formulas for the 2004 PS2 build were not audited.
core.implementation_or_verification: Store skills as versioned player stats with bounded curves and explicit save migration; test that UI, gameplay and save values agree.
core.scope: PS2 2004 baseline; source-specific platform caveats retained

core.topic: Melee as fictional gameplay, animation, and feedback
core.finding: [CONFIRMED] The manual exposes secondary attack and block/climb controls, but not the internal melee animation/state implementation.
core.implementation_or_verification: Use authored combo windows, stamina/cooldowns and hit-confirm events; test hitbox activation only during designated animation frames.
core.scope: PS2 2004 baseline; source-specific platform caveats retained

core.topic: Ranged combat as fictional gameplay, balancing, and feedback
core.finding: [CONFIRMED] The manual describes a first-person aiming mode for sniper rifle/rocket launcher equipment and separate target/shoot controls.
core.implementation_or_verification: Implement aim mode as a weapon-specific camera/input state; test zoom, cancellation, target loss and input priority.
core.scope: PS2 2004 baseline; source-specific platform caveats retained

core.topic: Inventory, fictional weapon classes, pickups, and switching
core.finding: [CONFIRMED] The manual documents weapon cycling controls and pickup/secondary interaction actions; it does not reveal the inventory data model.
core.implementation_or_verification: Use item definitions with category, ammo, animation set and HUD icon; test switching during reload and vehicle entry.
core.scope: PS2 2004 baseline; source-specific platform caveats retained

core.topic: Cars, motorcycles, bicycles, and other ground transport
core.finding: [CONFIRMED] The manual has separate vehicle controls for cars and bicycles; it also names special vehicle categories.
core.implementation_or_verification: Build ground classes with distinct controller tuning and a shared enter/exit interface; do not count a displayed mesh as a drivable vehicle.
core.scope: PS2 2004 baseline; source-specific platform caveats retained

core.topic: Aircraft, boats, trains, and other special transport
core.finding: [CONFIRMED] The manual documents aircraft controls separately for helicopter and plane, and describes water traversal controls elsewhere in the manual.
core.implementation_or_verification: Create separate flight and marine controllers; test take-off/landing or buoyancy modes independently from the car controller.
core.scope: PS2 2004 baseline; source-specific platform caveats retained

core.topic: Entering, exiting, customizing, damaging, and repairing vehicles
core.finding: [CONFIRMED] The manual assigns enter/exit to a context action and separates in-vehicle controls from on-foot controls.
core.implementation_or_verification: Implement a two-phase handoff: reserve seat/exit point → validate clearance → transfer input/camera → commit; rollback if blocked.
core.scope: PS2 2004 baseline; source-specific platform caveats retained

core.topic: Ambient traffic, lane behavior, navigation, and driver reactions
core.finding: [UNKNOWN] Detailed ambient traffic lane-selection, follow-distance and collision-avoidance algorithms are not established by the sources inspected.
core.implementation_or_verification: Use lane splines plus junction reservation and deterministic right-of-way; test opposing traffic and blocked intersections.
core.scope: PS2 2004 baseline; source-specific platform caveats retained

core.topic: Mission scripting, trigger logic, objectives, and state transitions
core.finding: [INFERRED] The number of contextual control sets in the manual implies multiple action maps tied to state, not one universal movement set.
core.implementation_or_verification: Use state-scoped input maps and mission triggers with idempotent event IDs; test event ordering and duplicate activation.
core.scope: PS2 2004 baseline; source-specific platform caveats retained

core.topic: Story structure, unlocks, progression, and persistent world changes
core.finding: [CONFIRMED] Rockstar's synopsis describes a story that starts with the protagonist's return and expands across the state; detailed unlock flags were not reconstructed here.
core.implementation_or_verification: Use a directed mission graph with prerequisite predicates, persistent unlocks and one authoritative progression owner.
core.scope: PS2 2004 baseline; source-specific platform caveats retained

core.topic: Main missions, dependencies, pacing, difficulty, and failure paths
core.finding: [UNKNOWN] A complete 2004 PS2 mission dependency table and all mission fail branches were not independently audited.
core.implementation_or_verification: Store each mission's prerequisites, objective graph, actor locks, failure reasons and reward transaction; validate acyclic dependencies.
core.scope: PS2 2004 baseline; source-specific platform caveats retained

core.topic: Side missions, services, races, and optional challenges
core.finding: [CONFIRMED] The manual advertises swimming, weights, boxing, martial arts and basketball as available activities/services.
core.implementation_or_verification: Represent optional activities as independent short-loop state machines with start, score, exit and payout tests.
core.scope: PS2 2004 baseline; source-specific platform caveats retained

core.topic: Collectibles, statistics, and completion tracking
core.finding: [SECONDARY] A current fan database lists 220 collectibles and 100 gang tags, but it aggregates the title across several releases and is not accepted as a PS2-only verified count.
core.implementation_or_verification: Track collectible IDs and completion categories independently; never import the current aggregate as the 2004 PS2 count without version verification.
core.scope: PS2 2004 baseline; source-specific platform caveats retained

core.topic: Money, rewards, shop transactions, and property income
core.finding: [CONFIRMED] The PS2 manual dedicates sections to money, shopping, gambling and services, establishing economy as part of the player-facing world.
core.implementation_or_verification: Use atomic purchase transactions: validate funds/stock → deduct → grant item → persist; rollback on any failure.
core.scope: PS2 2004 baseline; source-specific platform caveats retained

core.topic: Outfits, hair, tattoos, and appearance customization
core.finding: [CONFIRMED] The manual includes personal grooming services and explicitly describes changing CJ's appearance; exact option count is not established here.
core.implementation_or_verification: Build layered outfit/hair customization with slot compatibility and saveable appearance presets; test collision and animation clipping.
core.scope: PS2 2004 baseline; source-specific platform caveats retained

core.topic: Safehouses, properties, businesses, and indoor services
core.finding: [CONFIRMED] The manual lists accommodation and services, but this pass did not confirm every property or business system by build.
core.implementation_or_verification: Make safehouse/business ownership separate from entry/interior services and use persisted ownership IDs; test income idempotency.
core.scope: PS2 2004 baseline; source-specific platform caveats retained

core.topic: Game clock, day cycles, weather, and environmental state
core.finding: [SECONDARY] A former technical director recalled that separate city maps would have simplified different weather and emergency vehicles, but that was a discarded early proposal.
core.implementation_or_verification: Treat weather as region/sector data while keeping global time authoritative; test transition continuity rather than attributing this discarded concept to shipped behavior.
core.scope: PS2 2004 baseline; source-specific platform caveats retained

core.topic: Minigames, interactions, scoring, and rewards
core.finding: [CONFIRMED] The manual describes multiple activities, while the full mini-game inventory was not audited in this pass.
core.implementation_or_verification: Use minigame adapters that pause/open context safely and return reward/result events to the main progression system.
core.scope: PS2 2004 baseline; source-specific platform caveats retained

core.topic: HUD, minimap, map symbols, and objective communication
core.finding: [CONFIRMED] The manual gives a map legend toggle, zoom, pan/target and a navigational waypoint that appears on the radar; it also mentions territory and mission/contact map layers.
core.implementation_or_verification: Build full map + minimap from the same spatial metadata and route graph; test destination marker, route recalculation and save/load.
core.scope: PS2 2004 baseline; source-specific platform caveats retained

core.topic: Menus, settings, tutorials, accessibility, and usability
core.finding: [CONFIRMED] The manual documents the Start button pause menu and menu-based map access; it also supplies help through contextual controls.
core.implementation_or_verification: Use pause layers that freeze world simulation but keep menu input active; test audio pause and mission-save boundary behavior.
core.scope: PS2 2004 baseline; source-specific platform caveats retained

core.topic: Input, controller mapping, and platform behavior
core.finding: [CONFIRMED] The manual's NTSC-U/C PS2 edition maps locomotion and vehicle actions to the DualShock 2 sticks/buttons; this differs from keyboard/mouse.
core.implementation_or_verification: Create remappable Web keyboard/mouse bindings and state-specific action hints; do not copy PS2 key semantics literally.
core.scope: PS2 2004 baseline; source-specific platform caveats retained

core.topic: Saves, restarts, checkpoints, and state restoration
core.finding: [UNKNOWN] This research pass did not inspect save-card binary formats or fully enumerate safehouse save rules in the baseline build.
core.implementation_or_verification: Use versioned JSON/ConfigFile save snapshots with checksum, temp-write/rename and recovery from truncated data.
core.scope: PS2 2004 baseline; source-specific platform caveats retained

core.topic: Dialogue, subtitles, voice triggers, and localization
core.finding: [CONFIRMED] The manual includes positive/negative talk responses; the credit transcription includes voice-over production and dialogue-edit roles.
core.implementation_or_verification: Use dialogue events with speaker, line, subtitle, voice asset, emotion tag and localization key; test missing audio fallback explicitly.
core.scope: PS2 2004 baseline; source-specific platform caveats retained

core.topic: Radio stations, programming, playback, and vehicle context
core.finding: [CONFIRMED] The manual's radio listings expose station-specific programming/playlist presentation; credits identify music production and audio roles.
core.implementation_or_verification: Use original fictional radio stations and licensed/original audio bundles; test vehicle-context changes and seek/resume deterministically.
core.scope: PS2 2004 baseline; source-specific platform caveats retained

core.topic: World ambience, sound effects, Foley, and audio mixing
core.finding: [CONFIRMED] The PS2 credits list audio design and audio programming roles; the exact sound middleware and mixer graph are not established here.
core.implementation_or_verification: Build local Web audio buses by world/UI/voice/music/vehicle and apply distance/occlusion envelopes; profile concurrent voices.
core.scope: PS2 2004 baseline; source-specific platform caveats retained

core.topic: Cinematics: staging, camera, transitions, and synchronization
core.finding: [CONFIRMED] The credit transcription lists cut-scene animation, audio direction and motion-capture direction roles; this documents production specialties, not the runtime cutscene toolchain.
core.implementation_or_verification: Use timeline-driven original cinematics with deterministic player/vehicle lock and skip recovery; test save requests during playback.
core.scope: PS2 2004 baseline; source-specific platform caveats retained

core.topic: Secrets, cheats, glitches, and emergent interactions
core.finding: [SECONDARY] Developer recollection ties a persistent Bigfoot rumor to a mistaken interpretation of CJ's stomach-rumble sound; this is a retrospective anecdote, not a verified hidden creature.
core.implementation_or_verification: Keep easter eggs data-driven and distinguish ambient audio from world actor evidence; test that hints do not spawn undocumented entities.
core.scope: PS2 2004 baseline; source-specific platform caveats retained

core.topic: Runtime performance, hardware constraints, and stress cases
core.finding: [CONFIRMED] Former technical director says PS2 memory was tight; the developer Q&A also describes object-count limits per map section and 8-bit indexing in some structures.
core.implementation_or_verification: Use memory budgets by sector, capped populations, compressed assets and explicit overflow diagnostics; never infer the original's exact budgets.
core.scope: PS2 2004 baseline; source-specific platform caveats retained

core.topic: QA, regressions, version-dependent bugs, and validation
core.finding: [CONFIRMED] PS2 credits list a QA manager, test analysts, QA tools, standards testing and test/tool support roles.
core.implementation_or_verification: Automate deterministic scene tests and maintain separate manual visual/audio acceptance for areas automation cannot judge.
core.scope: PS2 2004 baseline; source-specific platform caveats retained

core.topic: Release history, ports, and explicitly scoped comparisons
core.finding: [CONFIRMED] Rockstar announced the original PS2 version as exclusive in March 2004, then announced PC and Xbox releases for June 2005.
core.implementation_or_verification: Keep PC/Xbox and later remasters in separate comparison records; do not back-port their renderer or input behavior into PS2 claims.
core.scope: PS2 2004 baseline; source-specific platform caveats retained

core.topic: Cross-system dependencies, player freedom, and design trade-offs
core.finding: [INFERRED] Context-specific controls, waypoint/radar, mission contacts and vehicle radio controls create strong dependencies between world, mission, input and HUD state.
core.implementation_or_verification: Use explicit state owners and event contracts; test a mission completion while driving, map updates after load and HUD refresh after a state swap.
core.scope: PS2 2004 baseline; source-specific platform caveats retained

graphics.topic: Art direction, visual reference, and composition
graphics.finding: [PROPOSED] Use an original painterly 3D direction with readable silhouettes, controlled value hierarchy and regional color scripts; test readability at gameplay camera distance.
graphics.implementation_or_verification: Create greybox-to-final art gates and review the same camera path in all four regions.
graphics.scope: PS2 source evidence where cited; original Web rendering choices are PROPOSED

graphics.topic: Rendering architecture and frame composition
graphics.finding: [CONFIRMED] A former technical director identifies RenderWare as the engine for San Andreas; the inspected evidence does not disclose its complete frame graph or PS2 render passes.
graphics.implementation_or_verification: Use Godot's Compatibility renderer and WebGL2; capture browser frames and profile material/overdraw costs instead of assuming parity.
graphics.scope: PS2 source evidence where cited; original Web rendering choices are PROPOSED

graphics.topic: PS2 hardware constraints and version-specific evidence
graphics.finding: [CONFIRMED] Developer testimony describes tight PS2 memory and per-section object ceilings; exact VRAM/EE/GS budgets are not given in the sources used.
graphics.implementation_or_verification: Set measured Web sector budgets for resident mesh, texture and NPC counts; add hard-budget CI stress tests.
graphics.scope: PS2 source evidence where cited; original Web rendering choices are PROPOSED

graphics.topic: Resolution, aspect ratio, display, and output behavior
graphics.finding: [UNKNOWN] Exact PS2 output resolution, aspect-ratio handling and region-specific display settings were not checked against a named retail disc/build.
graphics.implementation_or_verification: Treat output resolution as a tested export preset; capture at 1280×720 and 1920×1080 and verify HUD anchoring.
graphics.scope: PS2 source evidence where cited; original Web rendering choices are PROPOSED

graphics.topic: Coordinate spaces, transforms, and scene hierarchy
graphics.finding: [PROPOSED] Keep world transforms in meters, Y-up, and separate world, camera, local and UI coordinate spaces.
graphics.implementation_or_verification: Assert transform ownership and test world-to-map round trips at sector corners.
graphics.scope: PS2 source evidence where cited; original Web rendering choices are PROPOSED

graphics.topic: Spatial partitioning, scene queries, and visibility sets
